tools.name: get_user
tools.description: Get the New Relic user the API key belongs to (who am I: id, name, email)

body.query: query { actor { user { id name email } } }

tools.name: list_accounts
tools.description: List the New Relic accounts the API key can read (id and name), the account IDs every other tool needs

tools.name: nrql_query
tools.description: Run a read-only NRQL query against one New Relic account (e.g. SELECT count(*) FROM Transaction SINCE 1 hour ago) and return its results

account_id.description: New Relic account ID as a NUMBER, from list_accounts (e.g. 1234567)

nrql.description: NRQL query string, e.g. SELECT count(*) FROM Transaction FACET appName SINCE 1 hour ago LIMIT 20

body.query: query ($accountId: Int!, $nrql: Nrql!) { actor { account(id: $accountId) { nrql(query: $nrql) { results totalResult metadata { eventTypes facets messages } } } } }

tools.name: search_entities
tools.description: Search New Relic entities (applications, hosts, dashboards, monitors) with an entity search query, returning guid, name, domain, type and reporting state

query.description: Entity search query, e.g. name LIKE 'checkout' AND domain = 'APM' AND reporting = 'true'

cursor.description: Optional nextCursor from a previous call, to fetch the next page

body.query: query ($query: String!, $cursor: String) { actor { entitySearch(query: $query) { count results (cursor: $cursor) { nextCursor entities { guid name entityType domain type accountId reporting } } } } }

tools.name: list_alert_policies
tools.description: List the alert policies in one New Relic account (id, name, incident preference)

account_id.description: New Relic account ID as a NUMBER, from list_accounts (e.g. 1234567)

cursor.description: Optional nextCursor from a previous call, to fetch the next page

body.query: query ($accountId: Int!, $cursor: String) { actor { account(id: $accountId) { alerts { policiesSearch (cursor: $cursor) { policies { id name incidentPreference } totalCount nextCursor } } } } }

needs_review: NerdGraph is GraphQL-over-POST and spec v1 has no GraphQL type, so every tool is a FIXED read query sent as a POST body to /graphql, exactly as the committed monday.connector.json does it. Caller input never touches the query text: it is passed in the GraphQL `variables` object, where declarativeRuntime.renderBody keeps a solo placeholder's JSON type. Interpolating {{input.*}} into the document would let a caller close the read query and append a mutation, defeating the read-only (no write:true) intent of this spec.

nrql_query passes the caller's NRQL string as the `$nrql: Nrql!` VARIABLE, never as document text. NRQL itself is a query language with no mutation form (SELECT/SHOW only), and it cannot escape into the surrounding GraphQL document from a variable slot. What it CAN read is whatever the supplied API key is scoped to, which is a key-scoping decision, not something this spec can narrow.

account_id is declared as type number because NerdGraph types the account argument as Int!: a string would be rejected by GraphQL validation. A solo {{input.account_id}} placeholder preserves the JSON number through renderBody, so a numeric input arrives as a number.

GraphQL returns HTTP 200 with an `errors` array for query-level failures, so every tool picks `errors` through. Without it a permission or schema error would be shaped into an empty result and read as 'no accounts' (a silent-fallback falsehood).

pick keys carry the response path (`data.actor.accounts[]`, `data.actor.entitySearch.results.entities[]`) because applyPick sources an array from its KEY, not its value, so output keys read as the full dotted path. Functional but ugly; a spec v2 with a `from` on array picks would fix it.

base_url is the US data centre (api.newrelic.com). EU-region accounts serve NerdGraph from api.eu.newrelic.com, and an EU key against this host returns an auth-style failure rather than data. A per-customer region needs a base_url {fromCredential} variant, which this spec does not carry.

One request per tool (v1 limit) means no automatic paging: search_entities and list_alert_policies return a nextCursor and accept a cursor input, so a caller can page by passing it back, but the connector never loops. No clamp helper is used because none of these NerdGraph read fields takes a page-size argument (NRQL row limits live inside the caller's own LIMIT clause).
Field presence is taken from the NerdGraph documentation and schema, not from a live 2xx: no New Relic account was held, so the proof below covers wiring only, never payload shape.

What the shape-proof can and cannot say here: every tool posts to the SAME /graphql endpoint, so the SHAPE_PROVEN rows are one endpoint proven repeatedly (host, TLS, path, API-Key header). GraphQL document validity is NOT proven by them, because New Relic rejects on auth before it executes the query. Only a real key can prove the queries themselves.
